# Bug Report

## Summary

Describe the problem clearly and concisely.

## Context

Explain where the problem occurs and why it matters.

## Affected Artefact

Identify the affected component, document, model, POC, script, tool, or other artefact.

Examples:

- `docs/...`
- `pocs/...`
- architecture model
- Eclipse tooling
- Safety DSL
- MBSA Plugin

## Steps to Reproduce

1.
2.
3.

## Observed Behaviour

Describe what actually happens.

## Expected Behaviour

Describe what should happen instead.

## Evidence

Provide relevant evidence where available:

- console output;
- error messages;
- logs;
- screenshots;
- model extracts;
- validation results;
- commit references.

Do not include credentials, confidential information, private project-control material, or personal data.

## Environment

Provide only information relevant to reproducing the problem.

Examples:

- operating system;
- tool/version;
- Java version;
- Eclipse version;
- plugin version;
- repository revision.

## Engineering Impact

Describe the impact on engineering work, traceability, verification, validation, reproducibility, documentation, or users.

## Acceptance Criteria

Define the observable conditions required to consider this issue resolved.

- [ ] Root cause or failure condition understood
- [ ] Corrective change implemented
- [ ] Relevant verification completed
- [ ] No known regression introduced
- [ ] Relevant artefacts/documentation updated if required

## Related Artefacts / Issues

List relevant files, commits, issues, requirements, models, POCs, or other traceability references.

## Additional Notes

Add only information useful for understanding or resolving the issue.
